title: Minimum Cost Homecoming of a Robot in a Grid
summary: Consider an m x n grid where the robot starts at the cell (startrow, startcol) and its home is at the cell (homerow, homecol).
statement: Consider an m x n grid where the robot starts at the cell (startrow, startcol) and its home is at the cell (homerow, homecol). The robot can move in four directions: up, down, left, or right. Moving vertically into a cell at row r incurs a cost of rowCosts[r], and moving horizontally into a cell at column c incurs a cost of colCosts[c]. Determine the minimum total cost for the robot to return to its home.
constraints: Positions are valid cells; entering row r vertically costs row_costs[r], and entering column c horizontally costs col_costs[c].
All costs are positive, so an optimal route never moves away from the target row or column.
Return the minimum cost from start to home.
reference_solution:
def minimum_homecoming_cost(start_pos,home_pos,row_costs,col_costs):
    row,column=start_pos;target_row,target_column=home_pos;answer=0
    step=1 if row<target_row else -1
    while row!=target_row:row+=step;answer+=row_costs[row]
    step=1 if column<target_column else -1
    while column!=target_column:column+=step;answer+=col_costs[column]
    return answer

def minimum_homecoming_cost(start_pos,home_pos,row_costs,col_costs):
    row,column=start_pos;target_row,target_column=home_pos;answer=0
    step=1 if row<target_row else -1
    while row!=target_row:row+=step;answer+=row_costs[row]
    step=1 if column<target_column else -1
    while column!=target_column:column+=step;answer+=col_costs[column-step]
    return answer
hints: Positive costs mean detours only add entries and cannot reduce the necessary row and column crossings.
Walk monotonically from the start row to target row, then similarly for columns, charging each entered coordinate.
Choose step as +1 or -1; update coordinate first, then add its row or column cost.
Every route must enter each intervening coordinate at least once, and this monotone route enters each exactly once.
